cards.explanation: The answer is that some will abandon the faith. The Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith (1 Timothy 4:1). Paul isn't talking about a small stumble here, friends. He's talking about people walking away.

The answer is marriage and certain foods. Paul says these people will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods (1 Timothy 4:3). Notice he's naming two things people will forbid, and neither one is something he tells believers to give up.

The word is thanksgiving. Paul says God created those foods to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth (1 Timothy 4:3). Then he says nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected (1 Timothy 4:4). Thanks goes with the gift, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says, "For every creation of God is good…" (1 Timothy 4:4). He goes on to say that nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected. EVERY creation, friends. That's a big word, and it's the whole point.

The answer is the word of God and prayer. Paul says what is received with thanksgiving is sanctified by the word of God and prayer (1 Timothy 4:5). Two things, and they're both about God and talking with Him. A thankful heart, God's word and prayer all go together here.

The answer is False. Paul says, "By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus…" (1 Timothy 4:6). Timothy is meant to share them, friends, and he's nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction he has followed. Keeping them to himself isn't in the verse.
The word is godliness. Paul says, "Instead, train yourself for godliness." (1 Timothy 4:7). Notice the word train, friends. Godliness is something Timothy works at, like practice.

The answer is that godliness holds promise for this life and the next. Paul says godliness is valuable in every way, "…holding promise for the present life and for the one to come." (1 Timothy 4:8). That's two lives covered. Not many things can say that.

The answer is because we have set our hope on the living God. Paul says, "To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God…" (1 Timothy 4:10). The hard work rests on that hope. He also calls Him the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
The answer is his youth. Paul says, "Let no one despise your youth…" (1 Timothy 4:12). Timothy is young, friends, and Paul doesn't tell him to hide it. He tells him what to do instead.

The answer is True. Right after he says not to let anyone despise Timothy's youth, Paul says, "…but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity." (1 Timothy 4:12). That's five places to lead by example. Paul gives him something to do about it.

The word is Scripture. Paul says, "Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching." (1 Timothy 4:13). Reading it out loud for everyone comes first on the list, friends.

The answer is through a prophecy as the elders laid hands on him. Paul says the gift "…was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders." (1 Timothy 4:14). A prophecy and the elders' hands, both together. Then Paul tells Timothy not to neglect it.

The word is progress. Paul says, "Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all." (1 Timothy 4:15). Stay at it, friends, and people can see the growth.

The answer is False. Paul says, "Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching." (1 Timothy 4:16). Both get close attention, friends, and his life isn't said to matter less. I think a cookie that looks great and tastes like cardboard would teach the same lesson.

The answer is himself and those who hear him. Paul says, "Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you." (1 Timothy 4:16). Both Timothy and his listeners are in it together. Keep going, friends, because it matters for more than one person.
